sources.role: P4 consensus snapshots; P5/P6 matching actuals
sources.provider: FactSet Research Systems, Earnings Insight (weekly PDF, John Butters)

coverage.report_dates_with_pdf_capture: 454 (Wayback), from 2011-04-01; every month 2011-04..2016-12 and 2022-01..2026-09 has >=1 report (2022-02 none); 2017-2021 nearly absent from Wayback but present on the FactSet host for sampled February dates 2017-2019 (HEAD 200; host rate-limited further probing, HTTP 429)

sources.units: S&P 500 bottom-up EPS per index share (index points)
sources.definition: FactSet bottom-up EPS: aggregation of company-level estimates for current constituents (narrative: 'an aggregation of the estimates for all the companies in the index'); actuals on FactSet's basis. Pre-2012 reports use sector share-weighted earnings in $ billions, a different measure
sources.timestamp_semantics: Report date printed on each PDF (weekly, normally Friday); prices quoted as of the prior Thursday close; intraday publication time unknown -> would need the conservative rule 'available from the next NYSE session'
sources.target_quarter: Calendar quarter explicit in chart labels (e.g. Q116) and narrative; current quarter plus about 4-5 later quarters per report
sources.vintage_policy: Each weekly report is a vintage; actuals' first appearance as a solid bar is the first-release vintage (P6a) from 2012-10 only; earlier actuals have no archived publication date
sources.extraction: Per-quarter values exist only inside raster chart images; the narrative gives the current quarter's start- and end-of-quarter values only. Requires OCR or manual transcription of about 140 development-period reports
sources.permissions: Copyright FactSet, all rights reserved. Terms for systematic extraction not verified; not redistributed in any case
sources.missingness: Weeks missing in Wayback (1-5 reports per month captured); 2017-2021 host coverage unverified month by month
sources.rejection_reason: Matching actuals start Q3 2009, so the 32-quarter earnings warmup completes only around 2018-Q4 and the 60-month return warmup around late 2023, leaving under 12 development walk-forward months before the holdout. Also image-only values and unverified terms

sources.role: P4/P5 candidate (S&P operating EPS estimates and actuals, matched definition)
sources.provider: S&P Dow Jones Indices, sp-500-eps-est.xlsx (H. Silverblatt)
urls: https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/documents/additional-material/sp-500-eps-est.xlsx and three earlier URLs, via Wayback captures
sources.rejection_reason: Snapshots far too sparse for monthly consensus; current file holds only the current vintage. Realized operating EPS history (1988+) is on a different definition from any available dated consensus, so it cannot be combined

sources.provider: LSEG/Refinitiv (I/B/E/S) S&P 500 Earnings Scorecard, Lipper Alpha
sources.definition: Growth rates and share-weighted earnings in $ billions (per-share index EPS not confirmed)
sources.rejection_reason: History starts 2016 and is sparse until 2022; measure is not confirmed per-share EPS
Requires a higher paid plan (ACCESS DENIED); per-company current estimates, not dated index snapshots

sources.provider: ICE Data Indices via FRED (BAMLC0A0CM, ICE BofA US Corporate Index OAS)
sources.coverage: FRED: 'Starting in April 2026, this series will only include 3 years of observations. For more data, go to the source.'
sources.permissions: Proprietary to ICE Data Indices; reproduction requires prior written permission
sources.rejection_reason: Decades of OAS history not available free; using archived vintages would circumvent the provider's restriction; a yield-based spread (e.g. Moody's Baa minus Treasury) is a different definition and would need an amendment
